subject.title: Add atomic claim/lease primitives for concurrent cron job dispatch and removal

question: Which public cron concurrency contract should OpenClaw expose for safe removal during or around dispatch?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug patch; it creates public RPC, CLI, exit-code, and possibly persisted-state semantics that maintainers need to own before implementation.

options.title: Add narrow CAS/if-unclaimed remove
options.body: Add an explicit precondition flag or version check to `cron.remove`/`cron rm`, return a distinct conflict result/exit code, and leave full lease-token state out unless later needed.

options.title: Add full claim/lease tokens
options.body: Expose claim token, holder, and expiry state across show/remove/run payloads, accepting a larger public data model for stronger external coordination.

options.title: Document internal single-flight only
options.body: Treat `runningAtMs` as an internal scheduler guarantee and document what `cron rm` can and cannot promise without exposing a new removal precondition.

recommendation.title: Add narrow CAS/if-unclaimed remove
recommendation.body: Add an explicit precondition flag or version check to `cron.remove`/`cron rm`, return a distinct conflict result/exit code, and leave full lease-token state out unless later needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron Gateway schema/service work makes this the most direct API/product routing owner from the inspected history.
